paper_metadata.title: Seizure Relapse and Development of Drug Resistance Following Long-term Seizure Remission

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a consecutive sample of patients from a specialized center with well-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and a clear description of baseline characteristics. The recruitment period and setting are explicitly stated.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Our clinic serves a diverse patient population, including patients with new-onset epilepsy, easy-to-treat epilepsy, and drug-resistant epilepsy.
items.reasoning: The author describes the clinical setting and the breadth of the patient population served.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This study was performed on a cohort of 566 consecutive patients (≥12 years) who received newly administered AED treatments at the Epilepsy Clinic of the Rambam Medical Center between January 1999 and December 2005.
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive patients within a specific timeframe at a tertiary center is a robust method to limit selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between January 1999 and December 2005.
items.reasoning: The dates are clearly provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Epilepsy Clinic of the Rambam Medical Center
items.reasoning: The specific medical center and clinic type are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: 256 consecutive patients who entered long-term (>1 year) antiepileptic druginduced seizure remission were followed up prospectively... Eighty-five patients were excluded from analysis because they were either lost to follow-up within 24 months... discontinued all (1-3) new AED treatments... or had an uncertain diagnosis.
items.reasoning: The study defines the 'zero time' as the entry into 1-year remission and lists specific exclusion criteria.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of the remaining 481 patients, 256 patients (53%) entered long-term seizure remission (-1 year) and 225 patients (47%) continued to experience seizures
items.reasoning: The study accounts for the flow of all consecutive patients, and the participation of those meeting the remission criteria is complete within the cohort.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean [SD] age of the patients was 31.8 [15.8] years... Sixty-four (25%) of these 256 patients had generalized epilepsy... 71 had cryptogenic partial epilepsy, and 91 had symptomatic partial epilepsy
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical characteristics (age, epilepsy type, etiology) are provided for the analyzed sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study reports on those lost to follow-up early (85 patients), it does not provide a detailed comparison of characteristics between those lost and those who completed the study, which is a key requirement for low risk in this domain.
